subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Do maintainers approve replacing global inbound system-tag sanitization with provenance-marked inbound context plus queue-only neutralization of line-leading `System:` text for all prompt-bound system-event sources?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes where hostile-looking text is neutralized; source review can assess the proposed mechanism, but only maintainers can confirm the repository’s intended trust-boundary contract and accepted residual handling.

options.title: Approve the narrowed boundary
options.body: Accept the marker-based context boundary and queue chokepoint as the supported contract, with Doctor handling legacy persisted content.

options.title: Retain broader sanitization
options.body: Require a narrowly defined shared sanitizer for any external text that can reach prompts outside the system-event queue.

options.title: Split the refactor
options.body: Merge non-security label and SDK cleanup separately while holding sanitizer removal for a focused security design review.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrowed boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the marker-based context boundary and queue chokepoint as the supported contract, with Doctor handling legacy persisted content.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch author has the most direct context on the intended contract and can route the approval request to the relevant security owner.
